title: Biden announces US military pier to deliver aid to Gaza
body:
In his State of the Union address on Thursday 7 March 2024, US President Joe Biden announced that the US military would lead an emergency mission to build a temporary pier off Gaza's Mediterranean coast. The pier would receive ships carrying food, water, medicine and temporary shelters. Planning would initially be based in Cyprus. Biden said no US boots would be on the ground, so personnel would not deploy inside Gaza.

US officials said the operation would take a number of weeks to plan and execute and that Washington would coordinate with the Israeli army on security along Gaza's coast. Separately, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said a Cyprus-Gaza maritime aid corridor could open that weekend, with a test run possibly leaving Cyprus on 8 March.

The plan drew criticism. UN coordinator Sigrid Kaag welcomed sea access but said air and sea routes are no substitute for land routes. UNRWA argued that existing land crossings were faster, safer and cheaper. Mustafa Barghouti of the Palestinian National Initiative called it a diversion from starvation and cited a figure of about 700,000 people starving in northern Gaza. The US had airdropped 36,000 meals in northern Gaza by then, and on 29 February at least 112 Palestinians were killed, according to the Gaza Ministry of Health, as they waited for food aid.
